environment.network: Context offline; all HTTP(S) requests additionally blocked and logged.
limitations: Results describe this browser and renderer. Software-renderer timings do not establish hardware FPS or reliable speedup percentages.
Frame sampling stops at 60 intervals or an 8 second timer. A blocked browser task can delay the timer; sample counts are reported.
renderer.render() wall time is synchronous method duration, not isolated CPU time, GPU time, or complete frame-submission time.
A postprocessing pipeline can call renderer.render() several times per application frame. Method-call percentiles should not be compared as whole-frame CPU work against a different pipeline.

Denied camera access is injected through getUserMedia. The preview/modality fixture invokes the existing tracker state publisher without a MediaStream; it does not test a physical permission prompt or detector accuracy.
The fatal-recovery fixture injects a renderer-property failure during capture restoration. It verifies common failure presentation, not physical GPU device loss.
Keyboard, focus, and compact-layout checks are targeted integration checks, not a full screen-reader or accessibility certification.
Screenshot visual-review status is recorded separately from automated checks.

visualInspection.method: Opened every final screenshot and downloaded PNG individually in the image viewer; no generated image or composite is used as browser evidence.
observations: All three maintenance crew are visible in actual rasterized images as well as in the articulated-transform checks.
Cine, Studio and Alerta produce coherent and distinct lighting. Compact settings and the fatal retry state remain legible.
The higher-resolution Cinematic PNG shows clearer edges than the low-profile viewport and contains only the scene.
limits: The reduced-resolution orbit view still shows speckling/aliasing on very fine hatch detail. The separate surface audit investigates this; this report does not claim it is eliminated.
Automatic resolution changed during the software-renderer run. Captures retain their effective quality/DPR, and comparisons are not a controlled hardware benchmark.
Static screenshot review and short transform samples do not certify every possible temporal artifact or a photorealistic result.

targetedVerifications.purpose: Targeted verification of the five profile commits after fixing a QA frame-count race. No other integration scenario or timing sample is repeated.
targetedVerifications.method: A change listener registered after the application listener records the frame counter at the actual quality commit. Each observation waits for a strictly newer completed application frame.
warnings: Failed to create WebGPU Context Provider
targetedVerifications.reason: The original full-suite profile loop sampled its frame marker before the native select action. A frame could complete before the actual change event, allowing a profile observation to retain statistics from the preceding profile. In particular, the original balanced observation retained 160 draw calls. The test now records the frame counter inside a change listener registered after the application listener and waits for a strictly newer completed application frame.
targetedVerifications.scope: Only the five profile transitions were repeated on the identical frozen HTML. The original 12 integration cases, 146 checks, timing samples, 11 screenshots, four PNG downloads and their visual reviews remain preserved. The updated complete suite was not rerun.
targetedVerifications.supersedes: For frame-sensitive per-profile renderer statistics, use targetedVerifications[0].profiles in place of cases[id=quality-profiles].evidence.profiles. The earlier observations remain in the original case for traceability.
